cases.climate: Tropical monsoon; several crops per year; paddy rice

power.spatial_support: NASA POWER grid cell, ½° lat × ⅝° lon (MERRA-2 native); value describes the whole cell

soil.source: ISRIC SoilGrids 2.0 model estimate (250 m), 0–100 cm

suppliedAssumptions: Planting windows typed below are SUPPLIED TEST ASSUMPTIONS (as a farmer would type them); potato comes from the FAO Crop Calendar zone 9 (Old Brahmaputra Floodplain), a published calendar.
Crop history (Boro and Aman rice in 2024, with dates) is a test record.
Soil water capacity from the ISRIC SoilGrids 2.0 water-retention estimate (engine 1.3.0; no SSURGO outside the US, no soil test).
gaps: Soil water capacity comes from the SoilGrids 2.0 global soil model (a 250 m machine-learning estimate, not a measurement). A soil test of your field would be more reliable and takes precedence when entered.
Runoff is not modelled because the field's hydrologic soil group was not chosen; rain is fully counted, which overstates water on slopes and in heavy storms.
reviewQuestions: Does water soak in quickly (sandy), moderately, slowly, or very slowly (heavy clay) on this field? Choose the soil group in the comparison settings to model runoff.

Is there a market for each alternative crop near you?
Do these planting dates match what is practical on this field?
Is your wheat a winter (vernalising) type? If so, record it as "winter wheat".
